transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because flying has gotten a lot scarier for me than it should be. Just thinking about getting on a plane brings me back to this really rough turbulence on our honeymoon flight. I know people fly safely every day, but I still picture it happening again.
Does this anxiety happen only when you have to fly, or do you experience it in other situations as well?

Mostly around flying, or things that make me think about it. If I’m looking at flights for a conference, my chest tightens right away and I get this rush of panic—I just want to close the laptop. Even hearing a plane overhead can set it off.
Do you experience recurrent nightmares about that flight or sudden flashbacks where you feel as though you are back in that turbulence?
No, I don’t think so. I remember the flight when I start worrying about flying, but I don’t have nightmares or feel like I’m suddenly back there.
Aside from airplanes, do you experience similar fear or anxiety when using other public transportation, like buses, subways, or trains?
No, it’s really airplanes specifically. Buses or trains don’t bring up that same fear for me.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F40.0 as the fear is isolated strictly to airplanes and does not involve other forms of public transportation.
